summary: Supporters of Sheikh Hasina want her to return from exile in India.

title: Makers of GLP-1 drugs ordered to add warnings about rare eye condition that can lead to blindness
summary: The US Food and Drug Administration says Ozempic, Wegovy, and other weight-loss drugs must have labels about the condition, known as NAION.

summary: Slovyansk continues to be bombarded by Russian forces, making it almost uninhabitable with less than 10% of it's pre-war population remaining.

summary: Inflation has remained high, despite some easing in fuel prices caused by the US war on Iran.

title: French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies aged 104
summary: With 30 men under her orders, she organised sabotage operations, sheltered Allied airmen and joined the fight against the occupying German forces.

title: Nearly 64,000 flee Nigeria for Niger where a humanitarian crisis is deepening
summary: Violence in northern Nigeria is fueling a growing humanitarian crisis across the whole region: 64,000 have fled to neighbouring Niger and several hundred have left for Benin since the start of the year, as host countries struggle to cope, the UN’s refugee agency (UNHCR) said on Tuesday.

title: Egypt: Fact-checking site’s entire newsroom jailed as assault on press freedom widens
summary: Six journalists who make up the entire newsroom of the Egyptian fact-checking website Matsadash remain in detention, the UN human rights office (OHCHR) said on Tuesday, warning of proliferating assaults on press freedom by the Government.

title: Security Council LIVE: South Sudan’s first elections loom amid rising violence
summary: With South Sudan just six weeks away from its first national elections since independence, the Security Council meets in New York Tuesday amid deepening political uncertainty and worsening violence. Ambassadors are expected to press for an inclusive process and credible polls, while civilians bear the brunt of fighting, hunger and displacement.

title: When deaths go uncounted: WHO flags dangerous blind spots in Africa’s health data
summary: Quality health data can help authorities to identify emerging threats and take lifesaving action, but a new report reveals critical gaps in Africa’s health information systems.

title: Sudan war: First ‘suicide’ drone attacks, now long-range strikes are the norm
summary: Drones and drought are “closing in” on Sudan, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF), said on Tuesday, describing unprecedented attacks on the country’s infrastructure including by drones travelling up to 1,500 kilometres before hitting their target.

title: Climate crisis could push 141 million more women into extreme poverty
summary: More than one in three women and girls worldwide – roughly 1.5 billion – live in so-called “climate hotspots”, where high exposure to hazards such as cyclones and droughts combine with insecure jobs and deep gender inequality.

title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian boy in West Bank, health ministry says
summary: The Israeli military says its soldiers opened fire at individuals “who intended to hurl stones” at a road used by Israelis.

summary: The El Niño extreme weather pattern could cost the global economy up to $11 trillion and seriously impact food security, said the UN agency tackling rural poverty in developing countries on Monday.

title: COP31 opens in Antalya: Can climate promises finally deliver results?
summary: Nearly 200 countries have arrived on Türkiye's Mediterranean coast for a climate summit with a different ambition: fewer grand declarations and more concrete decisions. With a powerful El Niño threatening to worsen extreme weather, negotiators face difficult questions over climate finance, clean energy and how to protect communities already living with the consequences of climate change.

title: Security Council LIVE: Strikes on Ukraine’s power grid, as peace talks loom
summary: The Security Council met in New York on Ukraine Monday. Russian strikes on energy infrastructure are threatening millions with another cold, dark winter, and civilian deaths are climbing sharply. The meeting comes on the eve of US-backed talks due to take place in Abu Dhabi. Follow our live meeting coverage below.

title: Afghanistan faces deepening humanitarian crisis amid sweeping rights restrictions
summary: Afghanistan stands at a “difficult crossroad” more than five years after the Taliban returned to power, a senior UN official said on Friday. Relative stability and security are being undercut by a fragile economy, sweeping curbs on rights and acute humanitarian need.

title: From a ship frozen into Arctic ice, a warning to world leaders: Trust the science
summary: Drifting through the polar darkness, a team of scientists is documenting a rapidly changing Arctic. As sea ice retreats and oil tankers move in, a conversation with the UN chief reveals why the battle for climate science matters far beyond the North Pole.

title: Sudan’s suffering is plain for all to see say aid teams, as brutal war continues
summary: Aid teams working to help millions of people uprooted by the ongoing war in Sudan appealed on Friday for more international assistance amid desperate funding shortages, empty warehouses and overwhelming needs.

title: ‘No Escape’ for refugees on the frontlines of the climate crisis
summary: The climate emergency is an immediate crisis for refugees, with three in four – nearly 90 million people – living in countries facing high to severe exposure to hazards such as drought, floods and extreme heat.

title: World News in Brief: Korea tensions mount, UN demands answers over staff death in Yemen, Guterres in Spain, Nepal alert ahead of COP31

title: Abyei: Deadly drone strikes mark ‘new and concerning’ threat, UN peacekeeping chief warns
summary: Drone strikes that killed at least 30 people in Abyei last month have added “a new and concerning dimension” to security in the disputed area, the UN’s peacekeeping chief told the Security Council on Thursday.

title: Children at risk as war zone attacks on water and sanitation more than triple
summary: Attacks that damaged or destroyed water and sanitation systems in conflict zones tripled between 2021 and 2025, increasing children’s risk of exposure to disease outbreaks, malnutrition and violence.

title: UN peacekeeping chief warns of ‘security vacuum’ as Blue Helmets leave Lebanon and Western Sahara
summary: The UN’s peacekeeping chief warned on Wednesday that the withdrawal of “Blue Helmets” from Lebanon and Western Sahara risks leaving a dangerous security vacuum, while the Security Council remains divided over what, if anything, should replace them.

title: Gunfire damages tents at Rafah displacement site in Gaza, as aid teams prepare for winter storms
summary: Gunfire hit and damaged multiple tents at a displacement site in Gaza’s northern Rafah region on Tuesday, reportedly causing injuries and forcing a humanitarian partner to leave the area, the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) has said.

title: Fuel price shock: Why developing economies are paying the most at the pump
summary: When war shut the Strait of Hormuz in February, oil prices soared everywhere. But the pain at the pump has been far from equal, and the world’s developing economies are paying the heaviest price, according to a new report from UNCTAD, the UN trade and development agency.
